claims.text: The nanoparticles are equimolar CoCrFeNiCu high-entropy alloys.
The initial nanoparticles form a random solid solution.
Moderately elevated-temperature annealing under inert atmosphere promotes enhanced short-range order in these nanoparticles.
Lower-temperature annealing preserves relatively random chemical ordering with minimal short-range order.
Enhanced short-range ordering increases local binding energies.
Enhanced short-range ordering creates higher free-energy barriers.
The higher local binding energies and free-energy barriers retard thermally activated diffusion.
Retarded thermally activated diffusion delays the initiation of surface premelting.
Retarded diffusion and delayed surface premelting delay subsequent bulk melting.
Nanoparticles with enhanced short-range order will have a higher premelting onset temperature than randomly ordered control nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles with enhanced short-range order will exhibit a steeper and more abrupt melting transition than randomly ordered controls.
The proposed short-range-order effect should hold for equimolar CoCrFeNiCu nanoparticles approximately 5–20 nm in size under inert atmosphere.
Particle coarsening or oxidation may cause deviations from the predicted relationship.
High-resolution TEM and XRD can be used to verify and compare short-range-order levels in the two nanoparticle batches.
Differential scanning calorimetry can measure the premelting onset temperature and melting-transition steepness of the nanoparticle batches.
The hypothesis is falsified if the enhanced-SRO batch shows neither a statistically significant increase in premelting onset temperature nor a steeper melting transition relative to the control.
